Q: What is the significance of making a nested function global in Lua? A:

I looked at the Wikipedia article and your code, and I don't have a clue what that algorithm is doing, but I do know how defining Lua functions work.

Functions can be local or global variables; when you define function B inside function A, if you don't put local in front of the function definition, B is a global variable.

The other thing is upvalues. Every time Lua's control flow passes through a function definition, it creates a new "closure" of the function, with access to the local variables captured in that function (if there are any). (more info: https://www.lua.org/pil/6.1.html)

In your code, when B is defined as a global function, the global variable "B" is overwritten every time you call A. Then any further calls to B will call the latest definition of function B.

But when B is defined as a local function, it does not overwrite previous "closures" of B. Then any further calls to B depend on which closure of B is referenced.

Also note that if a variable is global, it does not become an upvalue (since accessing a global variable just means accessing that field in the _G table).
